## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests. ## Wiki index - [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md) - [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md) - [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md) - [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md) - [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md) - [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md) ## Main project file The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml). Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md) aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job. Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue. Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run. ## Shell timing When writing shell scripts, always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands. Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command; the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in interactive shell commands. ## Ideas Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under `./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as `ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`. ## Links in handoffs When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use the `codex://threads/` URL format. When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days. ## OpenCode GitHub Actions To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user. Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation. The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session, verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward. When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status. Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ` for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`, which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit. Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account. Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only. Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota. Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound. Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries. Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save. Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker. To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with `gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`, then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ` to discover the host and port and SSH with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper. When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when live log evidence can be collected. For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper: ```sh bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ``` The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from `_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while inspecting the runner. ## Mac SSH access The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as: ```sh ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p runner@.agentsweb.space ``` The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running. ## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`: ```sh bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub ``` For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and use the same key: ```sh ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \ -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \ -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \ -p runner@.agentsweb.space ``` Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never print secrets while inspecting a worker. ---PROMPT--- I want you to build a first-person shooter at the level of the most recent Call of Duty games. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project.

## Objective
- Build a polished browser game matching the one-line prompt: "2D Fortnite building inside a Worms artillery match".
- Deliver as a self-contained static web game with destructible terrain, Worms-style turn-based artillery, Fortnite-style grid building, strong visuals, HUD, sound, AI, and responsive/touch support.

## Requirements
- User gave no extra constraints beyond the game concept.
- Implemented per repo/environment guidance: static HTML/JS, desktop and mobile support, touch controls, visual browser verification.

## Decisions
- Plain static `index.html` + ES modules + canvas 2D; no framework/build step.
- Theme/title: “FORT WORM — Build & Blast,” parody crossover.
- Gameplay: 3v3 worms, 60s player turns, wind, destructible pixel terrain, wooden/brick/metal walls/floors/ramps, material harvesting, bazooka/grenade/cluster/pickaxe, AI storm squad.
- Canvas world is 1600×900; landscape uses cover-camera crop, portrait uses contain.
- Use procedural WebAudio; no external assets.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created full project structure and core systems:
  - `index.html`, `styles.css`
  - `src/main.js`, `src/game.js`, `src/render.js`, `src/terrain.js`, `src/particles.js`, `src/audio.js`, `src/logic.js`
- Implemented start screen, HUD, turn flow, AI, destructible terrain, projectile physics, explosions, building, harvesting, particles, sound, game over/rematch.
- Fixed runtime blockers:
  - TDZ error from `const game` during constructor event: changed to `let game`.
  - `buildCost is not a function` caused by accidental global canvas `window.game`: renderer now uses `ghost.cost`.
  - Charging added to `Game.update`.
  - Ramp fill drawn with local coordinates after context translate.
- Visual tuning completed:
  - Camera cover crop on landscape.
  - Start overlay lightened.
  - Explosion brightness reduced.
  - Build-grid overlay strengthened; build shockwaves reduced.
  - Terrain colors brightened.
  - Ghost pieces snap to nearby ground.
  - Build support gap calculation improved.
- Server running in tmux session `fortworm` at `http://localhost:3002`.
- Browser verification working via `playwright-cli`; screenshots saved under `screenshots/`.

### Active
- Verifying placed floor/ramp/building rendering at 1600×900 after latest fixes.
- Latest test placed floor at `(476,613)` and ramp at `(556,507)`; a wall attempt at `(700,590)` was invalid.
- Captured crop `screenshots/crop_builds.png` for inspection; not yet reviewed.

### Blocked
- Playwright environment runs slowly (~2–3 fps) due software rendering; game time advances slowly in real time. For verification, manually advance state with `game.update(1/60)` loops via browser eval.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `screenshots/crop_builds.png` to confirm ramp is now filled and floor/wall alignment looks correct.
2. Verify build placement, harvesting, grenade bounce/cluster, AI turns, and end screen visually.
3. Check for browser console/runtime errors after interactions; latest `favicon.ico` 404 is harmless.
4. Add automated logic tests (`tests/logic.test.mjs`) for helpers in `src/logic.js`.
5. Test mobile layouts at narrow/portrait and landscape phone sizes; adjust HUD/touch controls if needed.
6. Final screenshot review at 1600×900 and mobile, then stop tmux server and summarize.

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: all visual styling/responsive/touch states.

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: input, HUD binding, loop, touch controls.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/logic.js`: pure helpers to test.

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a polished browser game matching the one-line prompt: "2D Fortnite building inside a Worms artillery match".
- Deliver as a self-contained static web game with destructible terrain, Worms-style turn-based artillery, Fortnite-style grid building, strong visuals, HUD, sound, AI, and responsive/touch support.

## Requirements
- User gave no extra constraints beyond the game concept.
- Implemented per repo/environment guidance: static HTML/JS, desktop and mobile support, touch controls, visual browser verification.

## Decisions
- Plain static `index.html` + ES modules + canvas 2D; no framework/build step.
- Theme/title: “FORT WORM — Build & Blast,” parody crossover.
- Gameplay: 3v3 worms, 60s player turns, wind, destructible pixel terrain, wooden/brick/metal walls/floors/ramps, material harvesting, bazooka/grenade/cluster/pickaxe, AI storm squad.
- Canvas world is 1600×900; landscape uses cover-camera crop; portrait now uses a follow camera.
- Use procedural WebAudio; no external assets.
- Building grid changed to 80px; wall 80×80, floor 80×14, ramp 80×80.
- Portrait HUD moves material chips into a `#materialsDock` via JS; short-landscape HUD uses a compact one-row dock.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created full project structure and core systems:
  - `index.html`, `styles.css`
  - `src/main.js`, `src/game.js`, `src/render.js`, `src/terrain.js`, `src/particles.js`, `src/audio.js`, `src/logic.js`
- Implemented start screen, HUD, turn flow, AI, destructible terrain, projectile physics, explosions, building, harvesting, particles, sound, game over/rematch.
- Fixed runtime blockers:
  - TDZ error from `const game` during constructor event: changed to `let game`.
  - `buildCost is not a function` caused by accidental global canvas `window.game`: renderer now uses `ghost.cost`.
  - Charging added to `Game.update`.
  - Ramp fill drawn with local coordinates after context translate.
- Visual tuning completed:
  - Camera cover crop on landscape; short-landscape vertical bias.
  - Start overlay lightened; explosion brightness reduced; build-grid overlay strengthened; terrain colors brightened.
  - Ghost pieces snap to nearby terrain and existing building tops via `supportSurfaceBelow()`.
- Building system upgraded:
  - `BUILD_GRID = 80`; `SIZE.wall 80×80`, `floor 80×14`, `ramp 80×80`.
  - Ghost support snapping to terrain/building surfaces; AI wall x uses `-SIZE.wall.w / 2`.
  - Build-grid overlay reduced to ±2 cells.
- Responsive/mobile work:
  - Portrait follow camera implemented (`Renderer.portrait`, `cameraX`, `cameraFocus`), with scale `clamp(vw/520, vh/1180, vh/900)` and offset `vh*0.6 - 620*scale`.
  - Short-screen compact HUD (`max-height: 560px`) shows materials, one-row build/weapon dock, end-turn, touch controls.
  - Portrait material strip via `#materialsDock` relocation in `main.js`.
  - Verified portrait menu/game and landscape touch layouts via screenshots; look good.
- Added `tests/logic.test.mjs` with 11 pure-helper tests; all 11 pass with `node --test tests/logic.test.mjs`.
- Browser verification:
  - Harvest works (`+18 WOOD`, terrain carve confirmed).
  - Movement/jump/landing confirmed.
  - Grenade fires, bounces, explodes, resolves to `resolving`.
- Server running in tmux session `fortworm` at `http://localhost:3002`.
- Browser reopened and resized to 1600×900; console only shows harmless `favicon.ico` 404.

### Active
- Fixing critical cluster-bomb recursion bug:
  - `spawnBomblets()` creates projectiles with `kind: 'cluster'`; `explode()` spawns 4 more for every cluster, causing exponential growth.
  - Observed `maxProjectiles: 709`, `damage: 342`, `phase: 'over'` in one cluster shot.
  - Planned fix: set spawned bomblet `kind` to `'bomblet'`; update renderer cluster checks to include `'bomblet'`.
- Then verify cluster resolves cleanly, blast/building damage, AI turns, and end screen.

### Blocked
- Playwright daemon can hang on long eval loops; reopen with `playwright-cli close` then `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` if unresponsive.
- Browser is software-rendered (~2–3 fps); advance simulation manually with `game.update(1/60)` loops.

## Next Move
1. Change `spawnBomblets()` projectile kind from `'cluster'` to `'bomblet'` in `src/game.js`.
2. Update `src/render.js` cluster checks (`p.kind === 'cluster'` radius/colors and any other branches) to treat `'bomblet'`.
3. Re-run cluster test: expect no exponential projectile count, finite explosions, ammo consumed, phase resolves.
4. Verify wall/floor/ramp rendering at new 80px sizes and capture final desktop screenshot.
5. Test blast damage/destruction of buildings, AI turn flow, and game-over overlay.
6. Add favicon data URI to remove 404 console noise; optionally clear `terrain.scorch` on `generate()`.
7. Update `README.md` with game description/controls; run final tests and stop tmux server.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js`: gameplay, turn flow, building, projectiles; cluster bug and support snapping here.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/render.js`: scene/camera/worm/building rendering; portrait camera and build overlay.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: input, HUD binding, material dock relocation, loop.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: HUD, responsive short-screen/portrait layout, touch controls.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: DOM/HUD/start/end overlays; `#materialsDock` added.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/terrain.js`: procedural destructible island.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/logic.js`: pure helpers.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/tests/logic.test.mjs`: 11 passing helper tests.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/`: verification captures (`build_struct2.png`, `ghost_new.png`, `mobile_land_touch2.png`, `mobile_portrait_game3.png`).

## Important Context
- Run server: `tmux new-session -d -s fortworm 'PORT=3002 ./start.sh'`; currently running.
- Open browser: `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002`; screenshot: `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=...`.
- Canvas-only capture helper: `/tmp/capture-canvas.sh screenshots/name.png` (uses `canvas.toDataURL`, avoids screenshot timeout).
- Debug handle: `window.__fortworm = { game, renderer, audio }`.
- Build costs: wall 20, floor 15, ramp 25; build limit 4/turn; grid 80.
- Canvas waterline: `WORLD.waterY = 868`.
- `Game` emits events `toast`, `teams`, `refresh`, `turn`, `gameover`; `main.js` handles them.
- `newMatch()` does not clear `terrain.scorch` (array currently unused by renderer).
- Playwright default viewport was reset; currently 1600×900.
- Changes are uncommitted; repo initially only had workflow/helper files.
